forces.title: Expanding digital public infrastructure drives financial inclusion and data ecosystems
forces.description: India's rapidly expanding digital public infrastructure, including UPI, Aadhaar, Account Aggregator, and DigiLocker, is creating a rich real-time financial data ecosystem. This foundational layer supports AI-driven underwriting, financial inclusion, and hyper-personalized banking at an unprecedented scale, benefiting NBFCs and Microfinance by expanding access to formal financial services for millions of individuals and MSMEs. This ecosystem allows for more contextual credit decisions and efficient service delivery.

forces.title: B2B transactional inefficiencies and MSME credit gap persist
forces.description: Despite digital payment penetration, B2B commerce suffers from significant friction due to information asymmetry, manual processes, and disconnected systems. This results in an estimated credit gap of over INR 60 lakh crore for MSMEs, with smaller enterprises disproportionately underserved by formal channels. Delayed payments and locked working capital force MSMEs to rely on costly informal credit, directly compressing their margins and limiting growth, posing challenges for NBFCs targeting this segment.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Shift towards cash-flow-based lending for thin-file MSMEs via digital rails
forces.description: The inadequacy of traditional, collateral-based underwriting for thin-file MSMEs is driving a shift towards cash-flow-based lending. An interoperable digital layer (like ULI) can provide verified invoice and payment histories, enabling lenders to assess creditworthiness based on live business activity rather than past proxies. This approach reduces risk premiums, expands credit access to previously underserved MSMEs, and makes small-ticket financing economical, presenting a significant opportunity for NBFCs/MFIs to deepen penetration.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: RBI's harmonised framework boosts microfinance operating flexibility and growth
forces.description: The RBI’s 2022 harmonised regulatory framework for microfinance has provided greater operating flexibility, broadened the addressable borrower base, and offered more latitude in pricing and lending. This policy support normalized operating conditions post-COVID-19 and enabled a sharp revival in industry growth. It represents a significant structural enhancement, allowing NBFC-MFIs to expand and innovate within a clearer and more adaptable regulatory environment, contributing to sector recovery and disciplined growth in the long term.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: MFIN guardrails and credit bureau standards tighten microfinance lending discipline
forces.description: The introduction of MFIN Guardrails 1.02 and 2.03 has significantly strengthened origination discipline in the microfinance sector. Measures like reducing the maximum number of lenders per borrower, capping aggregate indebtedness, and restricting fresh lending to delinquent borrowers have curtailed overleveraging. Additionally, mandated daily reporting to credit bureaus enhances borrower-level data utilization for better assessment, leading to a healthier, post-guardrail portfolio and more conservative underwriting practices among NBFC-MFIs.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Microfinance portfolio clean-up improves asset quality and reduces stress
forces.description: The microfinance sector has undergone substantial balance-sheet repair through significant write-offs and Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC) sales during FY25-FY26, amounting to over 17% of the March 2024 loan book for CareEdge-rated NBFC-MFIs. This rigorous clean-up of legacy stressed assets, combined with improved collection efficiency and better-quality new originations under stricter guardrails, has led to a notable decline in Portfolio at Risk (PAR) across early delinquency buckets, creating a stronger foundation for future growth.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Technology-enabled credit assessment strengthens microfinance risk management
forces.description: The microfinance sector is increasingly adopting technology for credit assessment and monitoring. Greater use of borrower-level data, enhanced by daily credit-bureau reporting, enables lenders to accurately assess overall indebtedness and repayment behavior, thereby strengthening credit decisions and limiting excessive borrower leverage. Analytics and early-warning systems further aid in identifying and intervening in emerging portfolio stress, leading to more robust risk management and improved portfolio quality for NBFC-MFIs.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: NBFC-MFI business model diversification into retail lending segments
forces.description: A structural shift is occurring in NBFC-MFI business models, with a gradual diversification into individual lending and non-microfinance segments, reducing reliance on Joint Liability Group (JLG) based lending. The relaxation of qualifying-asset requirements from 75% to 60% facilitates this. Larger MFIs, with stronger capital and lower funding costs, are disproportionately benefiting, expanding into adjacent retail-lending segments. This trend reshapes competitive dynamics and opens new growth avenues, while concentrating non-microfinance AUM among larger players.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Uneven funding access constrains growth for medium and small MFIs
forces.description: Despite improved funding conditions for the microfinance sector overall, access to borrowings remains heavily skewed towards large MFIs. In FY26, large institutions secured approximately 98% of incremental borrowings, leaving medium and small MFIs facing constrained access and higher costs. This disparity limits the growth potential of smaller players, potentially leading to contraction in their balance sheets and further sector consolidation, posing a significant challenge to their sustainability and market competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Limited traction for CGSMFI 2.0 scheme intended to bridge funding gap
forces.description: The Government’s CGSMFI 2.0 scheme, designed to facilitate up to INR 20,000 crore in guarantee-backed loans to NBFC-MFIs, has shown limited traction. Actual disbursements are significantly below targets, with a sample of rated NBFC-MFIs receiving only INR 900 crore against an eligible INR 6,200 crore. This underutilization suggests the scheme is not effectively addressing the funding gap, particularly for smaller MFIs, potentially exacerbating their liquidity constraints and hindering sector-wide growth.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Government policy supports digital and AI-driven financial services
forces.description: The Indian government is actively providing strong policy support for digital initiatives, including UPI-based credit and AI-driven payments, alongside expanded financial inclusion schemes. These reforms aim to improve access, efficiency, and stability across the financial services sector. Furthermore, regulatory innovation and institutional initiatives are bolstering AI-driven financial services, contributing to a secure, inclusive, and technology-enabled financial ecosystem. This policy environment creates a conducive landscape for NBFCs to innovate and expand their digital offerings.

forces.title: RBI's unified framework enhances NBFC technology governance and cyber resilience
forces.description: The RBI has issued comprehensive Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework Directions, applicable to NBFCs among other regulated entities. This unified framework consolidates regulatory expectations for technology governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and information systems assurance. Key themes include board responsibilities, baseline controls, continuous monitoring, third-party risk management, and IS audits. This structural shift necessitates significant investment and adaptation from NBFCs to meet heightened security and resilience standards, impacting operational costs and strategic planning.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Consent-portable finance via Account Aggregator and ULI transforms lending
forces.description: The Account Aggregator (AA) and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) frameworks are revolutionizing financial data sharing and credit assessment. AA enables individuals and businesses, including MSMEs, to share verified financial histories across lenders with consent, reducing repeated onboarding. ULI, as a standardized integration layer, allows lenders to securely access diverse borrower data for faster, frictionless credit decisions. This consent-portable finance expands lending reach into thin-file and rural segments, directly benefiting NBFCs/MFIs by lowering acquisition costs and improving underwriting accuracy.

forces.title: AI-native financial services and embedded finance create new opportunities
forces.description: The convergence of AI, digital identity, and real-time payments is creating opportunities for AI-native financial services and embedded finance. AI-powered agents can automate cash flow management, risk assessment, and cross-border trade for businesses, while delivering personalized financial experiences for consumers. Embedded finance allows credit and financing products to be seamlessly integrated into digital platforms at the point of need for consumers, merchants, and MSMEs. This offers significant upside for NBFCs to innovate offerings and expand access across the economy.

forces.title: Capital raising constraints may hinder growth for smaller MFIs
forces.description: Following two years of losses, some Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) face significant challenges in raising adequate equity capital to fund their growth ambitions. A sustained improvement in profitability and healthy asset quality are crucial to attract equity investors back to the sector. Without sufficient capital infusion, these MFIs will struggle to expand their loan books, further exacerbating the uneven growth trajectory within the microfinance industry and potentially leading to sector consolidation around larger, well-capitalized players.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Deepening interconnectedness of NBFI sector within financial ecosystem
forces.description: The financial ecosystem is experiencing deepening linkages between banks, Non-Banking Financial Institutions (NBFIs), and private markets. This increasing interconnectedness across the system raises the systemic importance of NBFIs. With non-banking financial institutions managing 60% of financial assets globally, their role in financial stability and market dynamics is growing. This structural shift means NBFIs will face greater scrutiny and influence on the broader financial system, requiring enhanced risk management and regulatory compliance.

forces.title: Escalating cyber threats and regulatory focus on resilience for NBFCs
forces.description: The financial services sector, including NBFCs, faces escalating cyber threats due to growing digitization, cloud adoption, and interconnected systems, expanding the cyber attack surface. Regulators are intensifying their focus on cybersecurity and cyber resilience, given the rapid evolution of AI capabilities and potential threats. NBFCs must strengthen cyber resilience frameworks, invest in proactive risk management, and adhere to new RBI directives on digital payment security controls and technology risk, necessitating continuous investment and vigilance.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

viewpoints.title: Microfinance sector shows early growth revival and improved asset quality
viewpoints.description: The microfinance sector is exhibiting early signs of growth revival with increasing disbursements and Assets Under Management (AUM), following seven quarters of decline. Asset quality has also notably improved, especially in the post-guardrail portfolio, with delinquencies significantly lower. This suggests a healthier and more disciplined lending environment is emerging, bolstering the sector's recovery. CareEdge Ratings anticipates further moderation in credit costs, driving improved profitability for the sector in FY27.
viewpoints.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

viewpoints.title: NBFC-MFIs are leading the microfinance industry's rebound, gaining market share
viewpoints.description: NBFC-MFIs are at the forefront of the microfinance sector's rebound, demonstrating faster AUM growth compared to the overall industry. Their market share expanded significantly to 44% by June 2026, up from 39% in March 2024, primarily at the expense of traditional banks. This indicates a strategic shift and stronger performance within the NBFC-MFI segment, positioning them as key drivers for the sector's continued growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

viewpoints.title: Uneven funding access will concentrate microfinance growth among large MFIs
viewpoints.description: While funding conditions have generally improved for the microfinance sector, access remains heavily concentrated among larger MFIs. These institutions accounted for approximately 98% of incremental borrowings in FY26, leaving medium and small MFIs facing constrained access and higher costs. This disparity is expected to lead to sector consolidation, with larger, well-capitalised MFIs driving the majority of future growth, while smaller entities may struggle to expand or maintain their balance sheets.
viewpoints.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

viewpoints.title: India's financial sector transforming into an intelligent, inclusive ecosystem for citizens
viewpoints.description: India's financial services sector is at a unique inflection point, moving beyond traditional service delivery to actively construct an intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial operating system. This transformation, supported by DPI and real-time payment capabilities, aims to create a truly inclusive financial architecture. Success hinges on embedding trust, security, interoperability, and ease of access at every layer, making the sector a service-oriented system with the customer at its core and contributing to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

viewpoints.title: NBFCs expected to lead financial services sector profit growth in India
viewpoints.description: India’s financial services sector is projected to nearly double its profits by FY30, with Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFCs) anticipated to be the primary drivers, growing at an impressive 16% annually. This growth will be fueled by expanding retail credit, wealth management services, payments, and insurance segments. The strong performance forecast for NBFCs underscores their critical role in India's financial expansion and deepening financial inclusion across various income brackets.

viewpoints.title: NBFCs contributed significantly to India's record IPO fundraising in 2025
viewpoints.description: India's financial services sector, prominently led by Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFCs), played a crucial role in achieving a record-breaking year for Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) in 2025. The sector contributed to fundraising efforts that amassed approximately INR 1.95 lakh crore (US$ 22.55 billion) across 365 IPOs. This highlights strong investor confidence in NBFCs and indicates their robust business growth, attracting substantial capital market engagement and positioning them as key players in public market activity.

viewpoints.title: India poised to lead in building future-ready financial operating systems globally
viewpoints.description: India is uniquely positioned to capture a leadership role in designing next-generation financial operating systems, leveraging its strong digital public infrastructure, technology talent, policy ambition, and market scale. The country's demonstrated ability to build interoperable digital infrastructure for its entire population, while fostering innovation, provides a distinct advantage. This allows India to combine intelligence, trust, and scale to develop a model for the future of finance that could serve as a global benchmark, ensuring intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial services.
